identification.summary: ELUSIVE COMET is a name used by the Security Alliance (SEAL) for a threat actor that lures cryptocurrency professionals into fake interviews or meetings on Zoom and then gets them to grant remote control of their computer, enabling malware installation and wallet theft [S1][S2][S4].
identification.notes: The earliest dated reporting found is April 2025 (Trail of Bits post of 2025-04-17) [S1]; SEAL's own report date was not retrieved and earlier activity may exist. Vendor-style name; no Microsoft name or MITRE group ID was found in the sources consulted.

attribution.basis: Trail of Bits, as relayed by secondary reporting, linked the methods to the Bybit heist of February 2025, which public reporting attributes to Lazarus (North Korea) [S1][S6]. Other reporting says the campaign resembles activity previously associated with Lazarus but that attribution is unconfirmed [S7]. No government attribution of ELUSIVE COMET itself was found.

objectives: Financial gain: theft of cryptocurrency from individuals and executives, for example more than $100,000 drained from the wallets of Emblem Vault's CEO [S4][S8]. Reporting attributes millions of dollars in losses to the group [S8].

sectors: Venture capital and crypto media (as lure personas)
Cybersecurity vendors (Trail of Bits CEO targeted)
targeting.notes: Known targets named in sources are the Trail of Bits CEO (fake 'Bloomberg Crypto' interview request) and the Emblem Vault CEO [S1][S4]. Geographic scope was not stated in the sources consulted.

capabilities.summary: Social engineering rather than technical exploitation: operators approach targets on X, use Calendly links and Gmail addresses, join Zoom calls under the display name 'Zoom' so the remote-control request looks like a native system prompt, and exploit users habituated to clicking Approve [S1][S2][S9]. In the Emblem Vault case the victim was tricked into allowing a malware install; the payload was reported as GOOPDATE, which gave full device control and exposed credentials and wallets [S4][S10]. The attacker also took over the victim's X account to message contacts with the same scam [S10]. Zoom permits guests to request remote control by default, so success depends on the victim approving [S11].

campaigns.name: Fake 'Bloomberg Crypto' interview lure against Trail of Bits CEO
campaigns.summary: Trail of Bits CEO Dan Guido received an interview request appearing to come from 'Bloomberg Crypto' via X, using unofficial Calendly links and Gmail addresses; Trail of Bits identified it as ELUSIVE COMET activity and published mitigations on 2025-04-17 (PPPC profiles denying Zoom accessibility permission, a TCC monitoring script) [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Emblem Vault CEO compromise
campaigns.summary: Emblem Vault CEO Jake Gallen reported losing more than $100,000 in Bitcoin and Ether after a Zoom interview with an X persona posing as a crypto mining founder led to a malware install [S4][S10].

diamond.adversary: Unnamed operators tracked by SEAL as ELUSIVE COMET; sponsorship and nationality not confirmed in sources consulted; reported Lazarus similarities unconfirmed [S1][S7].
diamond.capability: Zoom remote-control abuse via social engineering; malware reported as GOOPDATE; account takeover on X [S1][S10].
diamond.infrastructure: Attacker X accounts, Gmail addresses, Calendly links and Zoom meeting URLs [S1].
diamond.victim: Crypto executives and security-vendor leadership, e.g. Trail of Bits CEO and Emblem Vault CEO [S1][S4].
diamond.technology: Zoom remote-control feature (default allows guest requests), macOS accessibility permissions, Calendly, X and Gmail [S1][S11].

provenance.importedSummary: ELUSIVE COMET is a threat actor responsible for significant cryptocurrency theft through sophisticated social engineering attacks, particularly leveraging Zoom's remote control feature. Their attack methodology involves manipulating legitimate workflows and exploiting human-centric vulnerabilities rather than technical flaws. The actor employs tactics such as social proof, time pressure, and interface manipulation to deceive targets. Organizations can mitigate risks by implementing technical controls to disable the remote control feature and deploying email boundary protections like DMARC, SPF, and DKIM.
